name: William Shakespeare
bio: English Renaissance playwright and sonneteer.
style: Dramatic turns, metaphor, and tightly argued sonnets.

name: Emily Dickinson
bio: American poet whose compressed lyrics explore mortality and inward life.
work: Because I could not stop for Death
style: Slant rhyme, dashes, paradox, and startling compression.

name: Robert Frost
bio: American poet of New England landscapes and difficult human choices.
style: Conversational meter, rural images, and unsettled conclusions.

name: Walt Whitman
bio: American poet who expanded the possibilities of free verse.
style: Expansive free verse, bodily imagery, and democratic catalogues.

name: Edgar Allan Poe
bio: American poet and fiction writer associated with Gothic literature.
style: Incantatory rhyme, musical repetition, and Gothic atmosphere.

name: Maya Angelou
bio: American poet and memoirist whose writing affirms Black resilience.
style: Direct address, rhythmic repetition, and defiant affirmation.

name: Langston Hughes
bio: American Harlem Renaissance poet shaped by blues and jazz.
style: Blues rhythms, colloquial speech, and Black everyday experience.

name: Sylvia Plath
bio: American poet whose intense lyrics transform personal experience.
style: Confessional intensity, sharp imagery, and controlled formal energy.

name: T.S. Eliot
bio: American-born British modernist poet and critic.
style: Fragmented voices, allusion, and urban spiritual unease.

name: E.E. Cummings
bio: American poet and visual artist who experimented with typography.
style: Broken syntax, playful typography, and intimate lyric surprise.

name: Wallace Stevens
bio: American modernist poet concerned with imagination and reality.
style: Meditative abstraction, sensuous images, and philosophical wit.

name: Allen Ginsberg
bio: American Beat poet who joined personal witness to public protest.
style: Breath-length lines, accumulative imagery, and prophetic candor.

name: Ezra Pound
bio: American modernist poet central to Imagism.
work: In a Station of the Metro
style: Precise images, compression, allusion, and juxtaposition.

name: Carl Sandburg
bio: American poet who celebrated workers and urban life.
style: Plainspoken free verse, public voices, and industrial landscapes.

name: Mary Oliver
bio: American poet known for close attention to the natural world.
style: Clear observation, quiet questions, and nature-centered revelation.

name: Anne Sexton
bio: American confessional poet who examined mental illness and domestic life.
style: Intimate disclosure, dark humor, and charged domestic imagery.

name: Edna St. Vincent Millay
bio: American lyric poet and accomplished writer of sonnets.
style: Musical formal verse, emotional candor, and independence.

name: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
bio: American nineteenth-century poet and translator.
style: Narrative song, strong meter, and memorable refrains.

name: Ralph Waldo Emerson
bio: American essayist and poet associated with Transcendentalism.
style: Philosophical paradox, nature symbolism, and spiritual self-reliance.

name: Shel Silverstein
bio: American poet, illustrator, and songwriter for children and adults.
style: Playful rhyme, absurd situations, and tender reversals.

name: Oscar Wilde
bio: Irish poet and dramatist associated with aestheticism.
style: Lyrical repetition, moral feeling, and polished verbal wit.

name: William Butler Yeats
bio: Irish poet whose work joins national myth and modern uncertainty.
style: Symbolic landscapes, incantation, and visionary historical patterns.

name: John Keats
bio: English Romantic poet attentive to beauty and mortality.
style: Sensuous imagery, musical odes, and suspended longing.

name: William Blake
bio: English poet, painter, and visionary printmaker.
work: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
style: Songlike simplicity, prophetic symbols, and social critique.

name: William Wordsworth
bio: English Romantic poet of memory and the natural world.
work: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud
style: Plain diction, remembered landscapes, and reflective inward movement.

name: John Milton
bio: English poet and polemicist of the seventeenth century.
style: Elevated blank verse, epic scale, and moral struggle.

name: Geoffrey Chaucer
bio: Medieval English poet who brought many social voices into verse.
style: Narrative variety, social satire, and lively speaking voices.

name: Percy Bysshe Shelley
bio: English Romantic poet of imagination and political hope.
style: Rushing lyric music, elemental imagery, and revolutionary aspiration.

name: Lord Byron
bio: English Romantic poet known for satire and rebellious heroes.
style: Conversational digression, biting irony, and restless romantic energy.

name: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
bio: English Romantic poet and critic fascinated by imagination.
work: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
style: Ballad rhythms, supernatural scenes, and dreamlike moral tension.

name: Alfred Lord Tennyson
bio: Victorian British Poet Laureate who explored faith and loss.
style: Musical stanza forms, elegiac meditation, and sensuous landscape.

name: Rudyard Kipling
bio: British poet and fiction writer associated with imperial-era literature.
style: Strong rhythm, direct address, and memorable moral narrative.

name: Dylan Thomas
bio: Welsh poet whose richly musical verse explores life and death.
work: Do not go gentle into that good night
style: Dense sound, elemental imagery, and intense patterned repetition.

name: John Donne
bio: English metaphysical poet and cleric.
style: Extended conceits, argumentative intimacy, and startling comparisons.

name: Gerard Manley Hopkins
bio: English Jesuit poet who developed sprung rhythm.
style: Stressed rhythm, compound words, and close natural observation.

name: Philip Larkin
bio: English poet whose restrained lyrics examine ordinary disappointments.
style: Conversational precision, formal control, and melancholy observation.

name: Ted Hughes
bio: English poet known for elemental depictions of animals and myth.
style: Muscular language, animal energy, and stark mythic imagery.

name: Robert Burns
bio: Scottish poet and songwriter who wrote in Scots and English.
style: Song rhythms, vernacular warmth, satire, and human fellowship.

name: Robert Browning
bio: Victorian English poet who developed the dramatic monologue.
style: Dramatic speakers, psychological tension, and revealing indirect speech.

name: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
bio: Victorian English poet whose work addresses love and social injustice.
style: Intimate sonnets, emotional argument, and lyrical musicality.

name: Christina Rossetti
bio: English Victorian poet of devotional and imaginative verse.
style: Songlike rhythms, symbolic detail, and desire tempered by renunciation.

name: W.H. Auden
bio: British-born American poet concerned with private and public ethics.
style: Formal versatility, conversational intelligence, and moral inquiry.

name: Seamus Heaney
bio: Irish poet whose writing connects rural memory with historical conflict.
style: Tactile language, rural labor, and layered historical memory.

name: Amy Lowell
bio: American Imagist poet and advocate of modern poetry.
style: Precise visual detail, free verse, and sensuous rhythmic pattern.

name: Wole Soyinka
bio: Nigerian poet, dramatist, and Nobel laureate.
style: Mythic allusion, dramatic voices, and resistance to oppression.

name: Derek Walcott
bio: Saint Lucian poet and playwright who reimagined epic through Caribbean experience.
style: Lush seascapes, historical layering, and classical forms reshaped by island life.

name: Geoffrey Hill
bio: English poet whose dense verse examines history, faith, and moral responsibility.
style: Compressed allusions, knotted syntax, and historical voices under moral pressure.

name: Thom Gunn
bio: English poet who joined formal discipline with life in San Francisco and queer experience.
style: Measured stanzas, bodily detail, and restrained tenderness amid urban life and loss.

name: Thomas Hardy
bio: English novelist and poet of rural memory, disappointed love, and an indifferent universe.
style: Uneven songlike meters, weathered landscapes, and skeptical turns toward fragile hope.

name: A.E. Housman
bio: English classical scholar and poet of youth, separation, and mortality.
style: Plain diction, ballad rhythms, and stoic endings that sharpen private grief.

name: Thomas Gray
bio: English poet whose reflective verse helped shape the graveyard tradition.
work: Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
style: Balanced quatrains, twilight imagery, and dignified reflection on overlooked lives.

name: Andrew Marvell
bio: English metaphysical poet and parliamentarian known for wit and political satire.
style: Ingenious arguments, elastic conceits, and swift shifts between desire and time.

name: Richard Crashaw
bio: English metaphysical poet of intensely sensuous Catholic devotion.
style: Baroque ornament, ecstatic repetition, and images of flame, wounds, and spiritual longing.

name: George Herbert
bio: Welsh-born English devotional poet and Anglican priest.
style: Conversational prayer, intricate stanza shapes, and humble objects turned into spiritual arguments.

name: Henry Vaughan
bio: Welsh metaphysical poet whose English lyrics explore spiritual vision and renewal.
style: Luminous natural images, memories of childhood, and meditative movement toward eternity.

name: Thomas Traherne
bio: English poet and Anglican clergyman who celebrated perception and divine abundance.
style: Expansive wonder, recurring images of light, and a childlike sense of limitless possession.

name: Robert Herrick
bio: English lyric poet and priest known for brief poems on pleasure and passing time.
style: Graceful short stanzas, floral imagery, and festive invitations shadowed by mortality.

name: Thomas Campion
bio: English poet and composer who wrote lyrics for lute songs.
work: There Is a Garden in Her Face
style: Musical phrasing, lucid diction, and compact meditations on love and transience.

name: Thomas Wyatt
bio: English Tudor courtier and poet who helped introduce the sonnet into English.
style: Taut courtly speech, restless rhythms, and guarded desire expressed through pursuit and restraint.

name: Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey
bio: English Tudor poet who developed the English sonnet and early blank verse.
style: Courtly restraint, balanced sonnet argument, and seasonal contrasts that expose private sorrow.

name: Edmund Spenser
bio: English Renaissance poet of allegorical romance and elaborate stanza forms.
style: Interwoven allegory, archaic diction, and richly patterned nine-line stanzas.

name: Philip Sidney
bio: English Renaissance courtier, poet, and defender of imaginative literature.
style: Self-questioning sonnets, rhetorical wit, and conflicts between reason and desire.

name: Michael Drayton
bio: English poet who mapped British landscapes and history in ambitious verse.
style: Personified rivers, topographical catalogues, and rolling descriptions of national memory.

name: Samuel Daniel
bio: English Renaissance poet and historian known for reflective sonnets and verse histories.
style: Polished sonnet phrasing, sober reflection, and controlled arguments about love and time.

name: Christopher Marlowe
bio: English Elizabethan dramatist and poet known for forceful verse and classical desire.
style: Sensuous narrative couplets, learned ornament, and a teasingly skeptical narrative voice.

name: Ben Jonson
bio: English Renaissance dramatist and poet who favored classical form and direct address.
style: Epigrammatic precision, balanced statements, and intimate feeling held inside formal restraint.

name: John Dryden
bio: English Restoration poet, critic, and translator celebrated for public satire.
style: Driving heroic couplets, sharply drawn portraits, and sustained political allegory.

name: Alexander Pope
bio: English Augustan poet whose satires examine taste, vanity, and social power.
style: Polished heroic couplets, mock-epic scale, and poised irony about social rituals.

name: Jonathan Swift
bio: Irish satirist and poet whose verse exposes vanity and everyday disorder.
work: A Description of a City Shower
style: Brisk couplets, concrete urban grime, and dry observation that punctures pretension.

name: Samuel Johnson
bio: English writer, critic, and poet who examined human ambition through moral satire.
style: Grave couplets, cumulative examples, and stern reflections on misplaced human hopes.

name: Thomas Chatterton
bio: English poet who created medieval-style poems attributed to the invented Thomas Rowley.
style: Invented archaic diction, dramatic medieval scenes, and youthful Romantic intensity.

name: Oliver Goldsmith
bio: Irish poet, novelist, and dramatist who wrote in English about social change.
style: Flowing couplets, pastoral recollection, and elegiac criticism of displacement and luxury.

name: William Cowper
bio: English poet whose verse joins domestic observation, faith, and humane reflection.
style: Conversational blank verse, homely particulars, and moral reflection unfolding through rural walks.

name: George Crabbe
bio: English poet and clergyman known for unsentimental portraits of rural and coastal life.
style: Plain narrative couplets, exact social detail, and compassion sharpened by harsh circumstance.

name: Christopher Smart
bio: English poet known for devotional verse and the visionary poem Jubilate Agno.
style: Litany-like parallel clauses, exuberant praise, and startling links between animals and sacred order.

name: Charlotte Smith
bio: English poet and novelist who helped renew the sonnet before Romanticism.
style: Melancholy sonnets, coastal and botanical detail, and private sorrow tied to public injustice.

name: Anna Laetitia Barbauld
bio: English poet and essayist whose work connects domestic feeling with public ethics.
style: Clear argumentative verse, prophetic historical perspective, and humane attention to ordinary lives.

name: Felicia Hemans
bio: English poet whose widely read lyrics explore home, loyalty, exile, and sacrifice.
style: Memorable ballad cadences, heightened scenes of duty, and domestic feeling tested by public events.

name: John Clare
bio: English poet of rural labor, local ecology, and threatened common land.
style: Minute field observations, vernacular turns, and intimate rhythms of belonging and estrangement.

name: James Macpherson
bio: Scottish poet whose English Ossian poems claimed to translate ancient Gaelic sources.
style: Rhapsodic prose rhythms, misty battle landscapes, and repeated laments for vanished heroes.

name: Thomas Moore
bio: Irish poet and songwriter whose English lyrics helped popularize Irish musical traditions.
style: Song-shaped stanzas, affectionate address, and national memory carried through wistful refrains.

name: Leigh Hunt
bio: English poet, essayist, and editor associated with the Romantic circle.
style: Easy narrative movement, genial directness, and moral feeling revealed through a brief encounter.

name: Walter Scott
bio: Scottish poet and novelist whose English narrative poems draw on border history and legend.
style: Galloping narrative meters, ballad refrains, and vivid historical landscapes of conflict and loyalty.

name: Robert Southey
bio: English Romantic poet and poet laureate who wrote historical epics and ballads.
style: Plain storytelling, recurring refrains, and ironic gaps between public glory and human cost.

name: William Morris
bio: English poet, designer, and socialist whose verse revives medieval storytelling.
style: Patient narrative verse, richly material settings, and yearning for distant worlds and fellowship.

name: Dante Gabriel Rossetti
bio: English Pre-Raphaelite poet and painter of intense symbolic and sensual scenes.
style: Jewel-like visual detail, medieval echoes, and desire suspended between earthly and spiritual worlds.

name: Algernon Charles Swinburne
bio: English Victorian poet known for virtuosic rhythms and provocative themes.
style: Surging musical repetition, elaborate rhyme, and classical images of passion and fate.

name: Ernest Dowson
bio: English Decadent poet of unfulfilled desire, fleeting pleasure, and regret.
work: Non sum qualis eram bonae sub regno Cynarae
style: Haunting refrains, languid musical lines, and repeated returns to an unattainable beloved.

name: George William Russell
bio: Irish poet, artist, and mystic who published in English under the name AE.
style: Visionary rural landscapes, luminous spiritual presences, and quiet lyric rhythms.

name: Edward Thomas
bio: English poet whose country walks register memory, hesitation, and approaching war.
style: Conversational pauses, exact sounds of the countryside, and emotion carried by understated observation.

name: Isaac Rosenberg
bio: English poet and painter whose First World War poems attend to bodily vulnerability.
work: Break of Day in the Trenches
style: Uneven speech rhythms, startling animal images, and dark wit amid material wartime detail.

name: Wilfred Owen
bio: English soldier-poet whose First World War verse exposes suffering and patriotic rhetoric.
style: Pararhyme, broken rhythms, and graphic sensory shocks that challenge ceremonial language.

name: Siegfried Sassoon
bio: English soldier-poet and memoirist known for bitter First World War satire.
style: Clipped narrative, harsh battlefield particulars, and sudden turns into accusation or dread.

name: Rupert Brooke
bio: English poet whose early First World War sonnets joined idealism with national belonging.
style: Smooth sonnet argument, idealized landscape, and intimate feeling expanded into patriotic vision.

name: Edward Lear
bio: English poet and artist celebrated for literary nonsense and illustrated verse.
style: Buoyant limerick rhythms, impossible creatures, and comic logic touched by loneliness.

name: Lewis Carroll
bio: English writer and mathematician whose poems explore nonsense and language games.
style: Invented words, exact metrical play, and absurd narratives built from familiar grammatical patterns.

name: Stevie Smith
bio: English poet and novelist whose deceptively simple verse explores isolation and death.
style: Nursery-rhyme cadences, abrupt tonal turns, and deadpan voices that unsettle everyday assumptions.

name: John Betjeman
bio: English poet and broadcaster known for affectionate attention to buildings and social habits.
style: Jaunty regular meters, architectural particulars, and nostalgia mingled with social comedy.

name: Denise Levertov
bio: British-born American poet whose lyrics connect perception, conscience, and spiritual inquiry.
style: Breath-shaped free verse, attentive line breaks, and images that open into ethical or spiritual questions.

name: Elizabeth Bishop
bio: American poet whose precise observations explore travel, displacement, and loss.
style: Exact descriptive detail, poised conversational syntax, and formal patterns strained by withheld emotion.
